pictures.scene: Carracci, The Holy Women at the Tomb — two full-length women standing on a dark bank before a mass of dark leaves and a brown cliff, one in a deep blue mantle over a red gown with both hands thrown up in alarm, the other swinging round with her back half turned in a great pale grey mantle over a green gown and a white headcloth, a third woman's face showing at the edge beside them and a strip of pale dawn sky with two tiny riders in the far country, early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, mary magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance, …
pictures.name: pd_carracci_holy_women_at_the_tomb

pictures.scene: Bogdanov-Belsky, At the School Doors — a ragged boy standing in an open doorway leaning against the jamb with his face turned away into the room, in a patched coat with a canvas satchel and a white bundle slung on his back, bast shoes bound to his feet with cord and a long staff under his hand, looking in at a lit schoolroom with a bench of small heads bent over their work, a blackboard, a map and a hanging lamp, he bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in, …
pictures.name: pd_bogdanov_belsky_at_school_doors

pictures.scene: Hammershoi, Sunlight — a wholly empty grey room with nobody in it, a tall white-framed window of small dark panes standing open to the light, a panelled door beside it, a moulded cornice along the top, and bars of hard white sunlight slanting across the panelling and falling in a bright wedge onto the bare grey floor, he entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there, …
pictures.name: pd_hammershoi_zonlicht

pictures.scene: Durer, Saint John Devouring the Book — a woodcut cut in dense black line all over, a mighty angel standing on legs like two pillars wreathed in flame with a radiant face ringed about with rays breaking through the cloud, holding down an open book which the kneeling John takes into his mouth, tall pines and a rocky bank filling the whole of one side, a second open book and an inkpot lying among the stones below, and small angels in the cloud above, then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_saint_john_devours_the_book

pictures.scene: van der Weyden, The Weeping Magdalene — one enormous bowed woman filling the whole frame against a flat burnished gold ground, her face bent low with the tears standing on her cheek, a crumpled white headcloth over her hair and a long white cloth hanging from her wrists, her hands clasped and wrung together in front of her, a grey-green gown with a jewelled belt and wide red damask sleeves, and at the bottom edge the pierced bleeding hand of the dead Christ, but mary stood outside the tomb weeping, and as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb, …
pictures.name: pd_weyden_tranen

pictures.scene: Bouguereau, Song of the Angels — angels in long white robes with great white wings standing close together under dark garden leaves, one bending her head over a lute, one drawing a bow across a violin with a gold band in her hair, a third at the edge with her face half seen, all of them with their eyes lowered and their faces quiet, and a fold of deep blue cloth in the corner below, and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet, …
pictures.name: pd_bouguereau_song_of_the_angels

pictures.scene: Millet, Man with a Hoe — one enormous full-height labourer standing straight up out of the broken ground and leaning both hands on the handle of his hoe, in a loose white shirt with the sleeves pushed back, a dark waistcoat, blue-green trousers and heavy pale boots, his lined face lifted and turned toward us, a pale grey sky behind him and a worked field of red-brown clods, stones and weeds spreading right out to the bottom edge, thinking he was the gardener, she said, sir, if you have carried him off, tell me where you have put him, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_man_with_a_hoe

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Noli Me Tangere — a fresco of a walled garden, the risen Christ standing barefoot in a long white robe with a gold rayed halo and a hoe over His shoulder, turning and putting out one hand to hold her off, and Mary Magdalene kneeling in the flowered grass in a pale gown under a wide orange-gold mantle with her long hair loose and her own hand reaching out toward Him, a woven wattle fence, dark green trees and a tall palm behind them, the whole surface finely crazed with age, jesus said to her, mary, she turned and said to him in hebrew, rabboni, which means teacher, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_noli_me_tangere

pictures.scene: Memling, Christ Blessing — one enormous half-length Christ filling the whole frame face on, His eyes looking straight out at us, long dark hair falling over both shoulders and a deep crimson robe, one hand lifted in front of Him with two fingers raised in blessing and the fingertips of a second pair of hands showing at the bottom edge, and behind His head a great burnished gold disc scored all over with fine ruled rays, ringed with dark blue cloud, jesus came and stood among them, peace be with you, he said to them, …
pictures.name: pd_memling_christ_blessing

pictures.scene: Bellini, Procession in Piazza San Marco — a great procession moving out across a broad square, rank behind rank of brothers in long pale grey habits carrying candles and staves, a gold reliquary shrine borne up on their shoulders, a red and gold canopy hung with painted shields going before them, and trumpeters, men in black gowns and men in scarlet standing round about, with the whole front of the basilica rising behind in dark domes, gilded arches, mosaic and the four gilt horses under a narrow strip of blue sky, as the father has sent me, so also i am sending you, …
pictures.name: pd_bellini_procession_piazza_san_marco

pictures.scene: El Greco, Pentecost — a tall dark vault filling the top of the picture carrying a white dove in a blaze of gold light, with small tongues of flame standing on the heads below, and under it a standing press of more than twenty, Mary in a deep blue mantle over a crimson robe with her hands joined and her face lifted, apostles round her in yellow, green, blue and grey with their faces turned up and their hands raised, one arm thrown up above them all in a blue sleeve, and several in the near front seen from behind in brilliant green, crimson and gold, when he had said this, he breathed on them and said, receive the holy spirit, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_pentecost

pictures.scene: van Gogh, At Eternity's Gate — one old man sitting all alone on a plain green rush-seated chair with his elbows on his knees and his two fists pressed against his face, his bald head bent right down so that nothing of his face can be seen, in a worn blue working suit buttoned from the neck to the ankle with heavy brown laced boots, a small red fire burning in the grate beside him and the bare boards of the floor worked in long strokes out to the bottom edge, now thomas called didymus, one of the twelve, was not with the disciples when jesus came, …
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_at_eternitys_gate

pictures.scene: Hunt, The Light of the World — one enormous full-height Christ standing at night outside a shut door that is grown over with ivy and tall dead weeds and has no handle on His side, in a long white robe under a heavy jewel-clasped embroidered cloak with a crown of thorns upon His head and a pale gold halo behind it, His bare feet in the grass and windfall apples, carrying a lit many-sided lantern low in one hand whose candle throws its warm light up over the door and across His robe, and raising His other hand at the edge of the frame to knock, with a dark wood of bare branches and a few stars behind Him, eight days later, his disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and thomas was with them, …
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: King David Kneeling — one great kneeling king filling the picture with his head thrown back and his eyes lifted, a tall jewelled gold crown on his red hair, one hand laid flat on his breast, wearing burnished steel armour over a deep red robe under an enormous gold cope stiff with embroidery and worked all over with small painted scenes, his harp leaning against him with a hand laid on its strings and one bare foot showing under his hem, a hand holding an open book at the edge of the frame with Latin lettering on its pages, and above him an angel in white flying down with a palm against a worked brown wall and a great red hanging, thomas replied, my lord and my god, …
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Velazquez, Saint John the Evangelist on Patmos — one huge young man sitting on a rock out of doors with a great open book held on his knee, in a loose white robe over a dusky rose mantle spread about him and a faint thin halo behind his head, his bare feet on the bare ground, his face lifted and turned up toward the light with his lips parted, holding up a white quill in his right hand with the first words already written across the page, a dark eagle standing in the shadow at his side, and far off in the corner of a dark sky a small shining vision in a blaze of light upon the clouds, jesus performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book, …
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_saint_john_the_evangelist_on_patmos

lines.text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance. So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, she said, and we do not know where they have put Him!
Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
The cloth that had been around Jesus' head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples returned to their homes.
But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
Woman, why are you weeping? they asked. Because they have taken my Lord away, she said, and I do not know where they have put Him.
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not recognize that it was Jesus.
Woman, why are you weeping? Jesus asked. Whom are you seeking? Thinking He was the gardener, she said, Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.
Jesus said to her, Mary. She turned and said to Him in Hebrew, Rabboni! which means Teacher.
Do not cling to Me, Jesus said, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, I have seen the Lord! And she told them what He had said to her.

It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. Peace be with you! He said to them.
After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Again Jesus said to them, Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.
When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, Receive the Holy Spirit.
If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.
Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.

So the other disciples told him, We have seen the Lord! But he replied, Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.
Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, Peace be with you.
Then Jesus said to Thomas, Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.
Thomas replied, My Lord and my God!
Jesus said to him, Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.
Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
